title: Gaurav Madaan Wins ₹1 Lakh on India's Got Latent After Viral 'Kamzoriyaan' Performance Stuns Karan Aujla
excerpt: The unknown singer's emotional rendition on Samay Raina's hit show left Punjabi superstar Karan Aujla visibly moved, turning an ordinary contestant into an overnight internet sensation.
body:
• Gaurav Madaan won ₹1 lakh on India's Got Latent Season 2 Episode 4 after his performance of 'Kamzoriyaan' went viral across social media platforms.
  • Punjabi superstar Karan Aujla, appearing as a guest judge alongside Tanmay Bhat, was visibly moved by Madaan's raw vocal performance.
  • The episode marks the latest viral moment from a show that has become the most-watched Indian streaming title of 2026, with an estimated 38.5 million viewers.
  • India's Got Latent Season 2 airs simultaneously on Netflix and YouTube every two weeks, a first-of-its-kind dual-platform simulcast for an Indian digital show.

An Unknown Singer Steals the Show

https://youtube.com/watch?v=mhOZE8G_uBk

In a show built on chaos, dark humor, and deliberately bizarre talent, Gaurav Madaan did something rare on India's Got Latent Season 2 — he made the judges stop laughing and start listening.

Madaan, an unknown singer with no prior public profile, appeared on the fourth episode of the hit comedy-reality show and performed 'Kamzoriyaan,' a song that drew an emotional response from the panel. The performance was striking enough to earn him the episode's ₹1 lakh cash prize when his self-rating matched the judges' average score — the show's signature winning mechanic.

But the real prize may have been the reaction from Karan Aujla, the Punjabi music superstar and one of India's biggest recording artists, who was serving as a guest judge on the episode alongside comedian Tanmay Bhat. Clips of Aujla's visibly moved reaction to Madaan's singing spread rapidly across X and Instagram within hours of the episode's release.

Karan Aujla's Presence Amplifies the Moment

Aujla, who recently collaborated with Ed Sheeran and is known for chart-topping albums like 'Making Memories' and 'Street Dreams,' brought significant star power to the episode. His presence on the panel — already generating buzz before the episode aired — drew a massive audience that amplified Madaan's performance far beyond the show's usual viewership.

"No private company in India has ever designed a show quite like this one — it's the only format where genuine talent and absurd comedy share the same stage."

— Industry observer on India's Got Latent's unique format

The episode also featured a power cut during taping, which Aujla handled with characteristic humor, joking to host Samay Raina about the show's production values. The moment became another viral clip, underscoring the unscripted energy that has made the show a cultural phenomenon.

India's Got Latent: From Controversy to Cultural Juggernaut

The show's journey to this point has been anything but smooth. Created by stand-up comedian Samay Raina, the first season launched on YouTube in mid-2024 and quickly built a cult following through its blend of dark humor, unfiltered contestant interactions, and celebrity roasts. But it was pulled offline in February 2025 after a controversy involving podcaster Ranveer Allahbadia's comments on the show sparked public and legal backlash.

Raina spent months in relative silence before announcing auditions for Season 2 in late 2025. The comeback was dramatic: a dual-platform simulcast deal saw the show premiere simultaneously on Netflix and YouTube on June 20, 2026 — a first for an Indian digital indie production. The premiere featured Alia Bhatt and Sharvari as guest judges and crossed 15 million YouTube views within hours.

According to Ormax Media's mid-year report, India's Got Latent Season 2 became the most-watched Indian streaming title of the first half of 2026, with an estimated 38.5 million viewers. On Netflix, it entered the Global Top 10 Non-English Shows chart, ranking seventh within its first week.

What Makes the Show Work

The format is deceptively simple. Contestants perform an unconventional skill, then rate themselves before the panel scores them. If the contestant's self-rating matches the judges' average, they win. The gap between self-perception and reality — often vast, sometimes surprisingly accurate — creates the show's comedy. Previous winners have included a UP police constable and a Donald Trump impersonator.

New episodes release every two weeks on both platforms, and Season 2 has featured guest judges ranging from Bollywood stars like Alia Bhatt to comedy veterans like Kiku Sharda, Vishal Dadlani, Raghu Ram, and Munawar Faruqui.

A Moment for the Diaspora

For Indians living abroad, India's Got Latent has become appointment viewing — one of the few Indian shows that works equally well for NRIs raised on Western comedy formats and those who grew up on Bollywood. The Netflix distribution makes it accessible globally, while the YouTube simulcast preserves the community-driven viewing experience that made the first season a phenomenon.

Madaan's viral moment is likely to be short-lived in the show's constant churn of memorable clips, but for one episode at least, genuine musical talent broke through the chaos.
nri_angle: India's Got Latent Season 2 streams globally on Netflix, making it one of the few Indian shows with simultaneous worldwide access for the diaspora.
